setlist_extra.title: That's It For The Other One

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (4 reviews): China Cat starts straight, then builds as the drummers swell the groove into a swirling descent; Reviewer picks China Cat as the best song of the show [4][8][14][15]
- **The Other One** (1 review, 1 other source): The uploader says this tape has the first correct lyrics to The Other One; Bobby forgot the lyrics during The Other One [3][8]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (2 reviews): Cryptical into The Other One is very tight, with electric intensity and Pigpen's organ [14][15]
- **Dark Star** (1 review, 1 other source): The tape lacks the opening bars of Dark Star; Phil asks for the light to be left on near its end; Short jams between the verses later appear in fully developed form on the Live/Dead version [1][4]
- **The Eleven** (2 reviews): The Eleven sounds primitive and hesitant and fades out at the end; Reviewer says this was the first time the band played The Eleven in public, explaining its choppiness [7][11]
- **New Potato Caboose** (1 review): Reviewer calls New Potato Caboose a classic bluesy version [7]
- **Born Cross-Eyed** (1 other source): A Spanish Jam tease follows Born Cross-Eyed [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Born Cross-Eyed**: rare: 14 archived performances [16]
- **The Eleven Jam Feedback**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]

## The recordings

- **gd68-02-03.sbd.jools.14987.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 9 songs; 41 min; rated 4.06/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds guitars and drums clear, especially for such an old show; Reviewer rates the sound C or C+ and thinks the tape runs slightly slow [5][7]
- **gd1968-02-03.sbd.miller.97346.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 8 songs; 60 min; rated 4.45/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: The first few notes of It Hurts Me Too are cut off on this tape [2]
- **gd1968-02-03.sbd.abe.4989.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 8 songs; 40 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [3]

## Around the show

- Deadbase IX lists a different song order, placing It Hurts Me Too after New Potato Caboose [3]
- Show falls during Anthem of the Sun sessions, and material from it was used on that album [14]
- Show falls during Anthem of the Sun sessions, and material from it was used on that album [15]
- Reviewer hears the band shifting from speedy psych-pop to acid-soaked improvisation [4]
- Reviewer finds the set typical of 1968 [5]
- First confirmed performance of The Eleven was 17 January 1968; 22 January 1968 also circulates [12]
- Reviewer finds the China Cat into The Eleven jams on those January 1968 tapes stellar though rough [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-02-03.sbd.jools.14987.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Julian (Jools) Elliott; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1968-02-03.sbd.miller.97346.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller [2]. Also: Source is a DAT from Rob Eaton, with pitch correction done with help from Joe B. Jones [2]
- **gd1968-02-03.sbd.abe.4989.sbeok.shnf**: source: CD > EAC > SHN [3]. Also: This release is the second half of a CD that also holds the 20 January 1968 show [3]
